failure_summary.description: Results were not bound and saved; two plans also omitted requested domains or a round-trip leg.
Agents ignored actionable updates, refined the wrong cached result, or searched again instead of filtering compatible cached results.
Hotel actions were omitted despite trip dates and an explicit stay duration grounding the hotel dates.
An arrival cutoff expressed as “by” was not encoded as a time range.

patch.reasoning: The skill already covers saving tool results, cache refinements, and complete domain/leg planning, so repeating those rules would not address a new gap. These edits resolve the conflicting hotel-date instruction for dates grounded in a trip itinerary and clarify how to encode a one-sided time cutoff.

edits.target: Hotel check-in and check-out dates must be explicit; do not borrow them from flight dates or infer a neighborhood.
edits.content: Hotel check-in and check-out dates must be grounded in the conversation. When a hotel is for a dated trip and no separate stay schedule is given, use the stated trip start date as check-in and the stated trip end or return date as checkout. If the user gives a stay duration in nights and a grounded start date but no checkout date, derive checkout by calling `adjust_date` with that date and the number of nights. Do not derive dates or duration from vague phrases such as “weekend getaway”; ask for missing dates when neither explicit trip dates nor an explicit duration determines the stay. Do not infer a neighborhood.

edits.target: - Validate value encoding as well as argument names. For fields documented as lower/upper endpoint lists, represent an exact requested value x as `[x, x]`; do not pass a scalar or singleton list, widen the value, or treat it as a minimum. Follow the schema for non-exact bounds and do not invent endpoints.
edits.content: - For time-of-day range arguments, encode an exact time `t` as `[t, t]`. Interpret “by t” as a range from the start of the day through `t`, encoded as `["12:00 AM", t]` in the schema’s time format. Apply the bound to the appropriate departure or arrival field, including when filtering compatible cached results.
